To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
syndecan- 2 is a key player in cancer progression and that it is regulated by the interaction between cancer cells and fibroblast-produced extracellular matrix.
the interaction of colorectal cancer cells with stromal fibroblas-produced ECM results in an increase of the expression of syndecan 2.

the interaction between cancer cells and fibroblast-produced extracellular matrix proteins leads to the upregulation of syndecan 2 expression and that this upregulation is critical for the adhesion, migration and organization of highly metastatic colorectral cancer cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of stromal ECM components and the syndecan family of proteoglycan receptors in colorectal cancer metastasis.
the role of the ECM in the expression and behavior of colorectal cancer cell.
understanding the mechanisms that regulate the behavior of colorectal cancer cells, which may lead to the discovery of new therapeutic targets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stromal fibroblas ECM components induce the expression of syndecan 2 in HCT-116 colorectal cancer cells, which is associated with enhanced cell adhesion, proliferation and migration.
the ECM proteins, fibronectins in particular, produced by the stromal cells are involved in the expression and activation of syndecan 2 in HCT-116 colorectal cancer cells.
the interaction between tumor cells and stromatal fibroblasts through ECM proteins is important for the development of colorectal cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
syndecan-1 and syndecan-3 expression is downregulated while syndecan-4 and syndecan 2 expression is upregulated by the fibroblast ECM and this is mediated through integrin alpha2beta1.
the ECM is an important regulator of cancer cell behavior, which is mediated by interactions between the ECM and the cell surface proteoglycan syndecan- 2.
the ECM proteins secreted by fibroblasts induce a shift in the expression of syndecan family members in colorectal cancer, which may have a role in the migration of tumor cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
syndecan- 2 is upregulated by fibroblast-derived ECM in colorectal cancer, and this upregulation is associated with increased cell motility and invasion.

syndecan-1 and -2 expression is differentially regulated in response to fibroblast-produced extracellular matrix and that this regulation may have important implications for the behavior of colorectal cancer cells.
